description: We are Conqueror, a team passionate about space exploration, science, and tech. For NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, we aim to build an interactive solution to monitor astronaut health during space missions, blending web dev, data visualization, human health, and immersive 3D. Driven by curiosity, creativity, and teamwork, we welcome motivated collaborators in code, UI/UX, 3D, data, biology, or space science to build with us.
summary:
M.O.O.N. (Monitoring of Astronauts’ Organism and Needs) is a web-based prototype designed to explore astronaut health and well-being during space missions. It brings together physiological indicators, health measurements, mission information and alert visualization in an interactive monitoring environment.

The project aims to make complex health information easier to explore and understand. Users can access an astronaut profile, examine health indicators, explore an interactive 3D representation of the human body and investigate how spaceflight can affect different physiological systems. M.O.O.N. also explores the use of simulation and rule-based alerts to help identify health-related situations that may require attention.

By connecting human physiology, space research and interactive visualization, M.O.O.N. seeks to support a clearer understanding of the challenges of maintaining astronaut health during long-duration space missions.
details:
1. Overview

M.O.O.N. is an interactive web application designed to explore astronaut health and well-being in the context of human spaceflight. It provides a structured environment for viewing astronaut profiles, exploring physiological indicators and understanding potential health-related changes during space missions.

2. Main Features

Astronaut Profile: Users can access an astronaut profile containing mission-related information.

Interactive 3D Anatomy: The application includes an interactive 3D human body. Users can explore anatomical regions and discover information about the physiological systems associated with them.

Health Indicators: M.O.O.N. organizes physiological and well-being indicators, including heart rate, blood pressure, blood oxygen saturation, body temperature, sleep duration, mood, blood glucose, respiratory measurements and physical activity.

Measurements and History: The platform is designed to organize health measurements and make their evolution easier to examine.

Alert System: A rule-based mechanism evaluates certain measurements and identifies situations that may require attention. Alerts are intended to support awareness, not replace professional medical assessment.

Simulation Environment: A separate simulation component explores hypothetical physiological scenarios and the generation of alerts.

3. Technology

The frontend was developed using React, TypeScript and Vite. Three.js and React Three Fiber support the interactive 3D experience, while Recharts is used for data visualization.

The backend uses Python, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy and SQLite. A separate FastAPI service handles simulation scenarios and alert evaluation.

4. Innovation and Impact

M.O.O.N. combines physiological information, anatomical exploration and interactive visualization in one environment. Its purpose is to make astronaut health information more accessible and understandable while highlighting the complexity of maintaining human well-being in space.

The project is an exploratory prototype. It is not a certified medical device and does not provide clinical diagnoses. Its longer-term ambition is to demonstrate how structured health data, simulation and visualization could contribute to astronaut health research and mission support.
